# Architecture

How mannn-hestia-proxy templates work internally.

## Template File Types

HestiaCP web templates live in `/usr/local/hestia/data/templates/web/nginx/php-fpm/`.

Each template consists of 3 files:

### `.tpl` — HTTP Server Block

Nginx config for HTTP (port 80). HestiaCP replaces `%variables%` before writing to disk.

```nginx
server {
    listen      %ip%:%web_port%;
    server_name %domain_idn% %alias_idn%;

    # Include proxy config generated by .sh
    include %home%/%user%/conf/web/%domain%/nginx.proxy.conf;

    # Standard HestiaCP includes
    include %home%/%user%/conf/web/%domain%/nginx.conf_*;
}
```

Available variables:
| Variable | Replaced With |
|----------|--------------|
| `%ip%` | Server IP |
| `%web_port%` | HTTP port (usually 80) |
| `%web_ssl_port%` | HTTPS port (usually 443) |
| `%domain_idn%` | Domain name (IDN encoded) |
| `%alias_idn%` | Domain aliases |
| `%user%` | HestiaCP username |
| `%home%` | Home directory base (usually `/home`) |
| `%docroot%` | Document root path |
| `%ssl_pem%` | SSL certificate path |
| `%ssl_key%` | SSL private key path |

### `.stpl` — HTTPS Server Block

Same as `.tpl` but with SSL directives. Includes `nginx.proxy.ssl.conf` instead of `nginx.proxy.conf`.

### `.sh` — Shell Script (runs on template apply)

Executed by HestiaCP as **root** when the template is applied or re-applied.

Receives 5 positional arguments:
| Arg | Variable | Example |
|-----|----------|---------|
| `$1` | user | `myuser` |
| `$2` | domain | `api.example.com` |
| `$3` | ip | `203.0.113.10` |
| `$4` | home | `/home` |
| `$5` | docroot | `/home/myuser/web/api.example.com/public_html` |

**Important**: `%variables%` are NOT available in `.sh` files. Use positional args only.

## What .sh Does (execution order)

```
1. Create app directory        → mkdir -p, chown, chmod
2. Create default .env         → runtime-specific safe default port
3. Create placeholder code     → server.js / main.go / app.py (if not exists)
4. Go: auto-compile            → runuser as domain user (go build -o server)
5. Validate PORT from .env     → allow only runtime-specific safe port range
6. Register port               → port registry acquire/migrate (release old port + firewall rules)
7. Generate nginx proxy config → nginx.proxy.conf + nginx.proxy.ssl.conf
8. Create unique systemd service → /etc/systemd/system/mannn-{user}-{hash}.service
9. Enable + start service      → systemctl enable + start (or restart)
10. Restrict port in firewall  → DROP ! -i lo rule on iptables AND ip6tables, tagged mannn-<user>-<domainhash>-<port>

If the requested PORT is already registered to a different service unit, the script writes
a 503 stub config for the domain, does not start the service, and exits with an error
telling the user to change PORT in .env and re-apply.

Docker backend mode is the exception: it only writes nginx proxy files from `BACKEND_PORT` and does not create a Docker service.
```

## Dynamic Proxy Pattern

Traditional approach: one template per port (static).
```
template-nodejs-3100.tpl → proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3100
template-nodejs-3101.tpl → proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3101
```

mannn-hestia-proxy approach: one template, port from .env (dynamic).
```
template applies → .sh reads .env PORT → generates include file → nginx loads it
```

The `.tpl`/`.stpl` use `include` to load a generated config file:
```nginx
include %home%/%user%/conf/web/%domain%/nginx.proxy.conf;
```

This file is generated by `.sh` with the correct port from `.env`.

## File Locations

After template is applied to domain `api.example.com` for user `myuser`:

```
/home/myuser/
├── conf/web/api.example.com/
│   ├── nginx.conf              ← main nginx config (HestiaCP managed)
│   ├── nginx.proxy.conf        ← HTTP proxy include (generated by .sh)
│   └── nginx.proxy.ssl.conf    ← HTTPS proxy include (generated by .sh)
└── web/api.example.com/
    └── private/
        └── nodejs/              ← app directory
            ├── .env             ← PORT=3100
            └── server.js        ← app code

/etc/systemd/system/
└── mannn-myuser-a1b2c3d4e5f6.service  ← auto-created systemd service
```

## Generated Systemd Service

Naming: `mannn-{user}-{hash(domain)}` to prevent collisions between similar domain strings.

Example for user `myuser` and `api.example.com` → `mannn-myuser-a1b2c3d4e5f6.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Node.js app for api.example.com
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=myuser
Group=myuser
WorkingDirectory=/home/myuser/web/api.example.com/private/nodejs
ExecStart=/usr/local/node/bin/node server.js
Restart=on-failure
TimeoutStopSec=20
RestartSec=5
Environment=NODE_ENV=production
Environment=PORT=3100
# Systemd sandbox hardening
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ProtectClock=yes
ProtectControlGroups=yes
ProtectHostname=yes
ProtectKernelLogs=yes
ProtectKernelModules=yes
ProtectKernelTunables=yes
ProtectProc=invisible
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_NETLINK
RestrictRealtime=yes
RestrictSUIDSGID=yes
SystemCallArchitectures=native
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
SystemCallErrorNumber=EPERM
LockPersonality=yes
MemoryMax=512M
UMask=0027
ReadWritePaths=/home/myuser/web/api.example.com/private/nodejs
CapabilityBoundingSet=
AmbientCapabilities=

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

`MemoryMax` defaults per runtime: node `512M`, go `256M`, python `512M`, frankenphp `1G`.
Tune per app with a drop-in — it survives re-apply:

```bash
# /etc/systemd/system/mannn-<user>-<hash>.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
MemoryMax=2G
```
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

## Proxy Headers

All proxy configs pass these headers to the backend app:

| Header | Value | Purpose |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `Host` | `$host` | Original domain name |
| `X-Real-IP` | `$remote_addr` | Client's real IP |
| `X-Forwarded-For` | `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` | Proxy chain IPs |
| `X-Forwarded-Proto` | `$scheme` / `https` | Original protocol |
| `X-Forwarded-Host` | `$host` | Original host requested by the client |
| `X-Forwarded-Port` | `$server_port` | Original port requested by the client |
| `Upgrade` | `$http_upgrade` | WebSocket support |
| `Connection` | `$connection_upgrade` | WebSocket support via shared upgrade map |
| `Early-Data` | `$rfc_early_data` | SSL templates only — lets the backend detect TLS 1.3 0-RTT replays (RFC 8470); omitted unless the request used early data |

The `Connection` header uses `$connection_upgrade`, defined by a shared map deployed to
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/mannn-upgrade-map.conf`:

```nginx
map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
    default upgrade;
    ""      close;
}
```

This sends `Connection: upgrade` only for real upgrade requests and `close` otherwise
(previously hardcoded `"upgrade"` on every request).

Timeouts: connect/send stay 60s; `proxy_read_timeout` is 3600s so idle WebSocket
connections survive, and `proxy_buffering` is off so SSE/streaming responses are not
buffered.

## Security Headers

All templates include these response headers applied at the nginx layer:

| Header | Value | Scope |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `X-Frame-Options` | `SAMEORIGIN` | All templates |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | All templates |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | All templates |
| `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` | `frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'` | All templates — report-only so apps can set their own enforcing CSP without double-policy breakage |
| `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()` | All templates |
| `proxy_hide_header` | `X-Powered-By` | All templates — prevents backend technology disclosure (e.g. `PHP/8.x.x`) |

Removed in this version: the legacy XSS auditor header (obsolete and harmful on old
browsers) and the hardcoded `Strict-Transport-Security` — HSTS is now solely managed via
the HestiaCP panel (`nginx.hsts.conf` include), avoiding duplicate STS headers.

## Sensitive File Blocking

All templates include location blocks that return 404 at the nginx layer, before the request reaches the backend:

```nginx
# Block sensitive file extensions
location ~* \.(bak|backup|old|orig|save|swp|tmp|sql|zip|tar|gz|rar|log)(\.gz)?$ {
    return 404;
}

# Block common config file paths
location ~* ^/(wp-config\.php|config\.php|settings\.php|database\.yml|appsettings\.json)$ {
    return 404;
}
```

This prevents:
- **Soft 404 attacks** — backends that return 200 for all paths (catch-all/SPA handlers) no longer expose sensitive file paths
- **Automated scanning** — tools scanning for `wp-config.php.bak`, `.env.backup`, etc. get proper 404 responses
- **Information leakage** — backup files, database dumps, log files are blocked at the edge

## Rate Limiting

A shared rate limit zone is deployed to `/etc/nginx/conf.d/mannn-rate-limit.conf`:

```nginx
limit_req_zone $server_name$binary_remote_addr zone=mannn:10m rate=10r/s;
```

All templates reference this zone:

```nginx
# dynamic requests (server level in every mannn template)
limit_req zone=mannn burst=20 nodelay;
# static asset locations override with the loose zone
limit_req zone=mannn_static burst=100 nodelay;
```

- **10 MB shared memory** — tracks ~160k unique domain+IP keys
- **10 requests/second** per domain per IP with burst allowance of 20 (rate unchanged)
- **per-domain key** (`$server_name$binary_remote_addr`) — traffic to one domain no longer consumes another domain's budget for the same client IP; important behind shared NAT (offices, universities, mobile carriers)
- **`nodelay`** — processes burst immediately, rejecting excess
- **HTTP 429** — rejected requests return 429 (Too Many Requests) instead of the default 503
- **static assets are exempt from the strict zone** (`mannn_static`, 100 r/s): a dashboard page load pulls 50+ js/css/svg files in one burst and must not hang the page loader. CONVENTION: never apply the strict zone to asset locations; keep brute-force protection on dynamic routes only

## Additional Hardening

| Directive | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `server_tokens` | `off` | Hides nginx version from `Server:` header and error pages |
| `client_max_body_size` | `10m` | Limits request body to 10MB — prevents oversized uploads |


## TLS (SSL templates)

- `http2 on;` directive instead of the deprecated `listen ... http2` flag (nginx ≥ 1.25.1)
- OCSP stapling removed — Let's Encrypt ends OCSP support in 2025; matches upstream HestiaCP
- TLS 1.3 0-RTT anti-replay handling (`$anti_replay`) like upstream HestiaCP templates, plus `Early-Data: 1` forwarded to the backend (RFC 8470) so apps can reject non-idempotent early-data replays
- `/vstats/` location restored so domain statistics keep working

## Port Registry

Every used port is registered in `/usr/local/hestia/data/mannn-ports/<port>`; the file
content is the owning systemd service unit name.

- Acquiring a port already registered to a **different** unit fails (previously two domains
  of the same runtime could silently share a port, routing both to one app)
- The failed domain gets a temporary 503 stub config, its service is not started, and the
  error instructs the user to change `PORT` in `.env` and re-apply
- Changing `PORT` migrates the registry entry and removes the old firewall rules (both families)
- Registry mutations are serialized with `flock` (`mannn-ports/.lock`), so concurrent applies
  of the same domain can never interleave release/acquire
- The registry directory is root-only (`700`, files `600`) — it maps unit names to ports and
  must not leak to unprivileged local users
- Full uninstall releases every registry entry, flushes every `mannn-*` firewall rule (IPv4
  and IPv6, including legacy `! -s` rules from older versions), and stops every `mannn-*`
  systemd service

## Re-applying Template

When you re-apply a template (`v-change-web-domain-tpl`):

- `.sh` runs again from scratch
- `.env` — **preserved** if already exists
- App code — **preserved** if files exist (placeholder only created when no files found)
- nginx proxy config — **regenerated** from current .env PORT
- Systemd service — **regenerated** and restarted (or started if new)
- Go binary — **rebuilt** only if no binary exists and main.go exists

This means re-applying is safe — it won't overwrite your app code.


## Security Hardening

All runtime templates source a shared helper file `mannn-security.sh` during installation. The helper provides:

- collision-safe service/container naming based on `user + sha256(domain)`
- blocked-port enforcement for control-plane and common infrastructure ports
- per-runtime localhost port allowlists
- the port registry (acquire/migrate/release) that prevents two domains from sharing a port
- iptables port restriction — DROP `! -i lo` rules commented `mannn-<user>-<domainhash>-<port>`, auto-removed on port change and uninstall
- Go compilation as the domain user via `runuser` (HOME set to the app dir, build cache under `private/go/.cache`) — root never compiles user-supplied code
- basic symlink rejection before root writes files

### Docker hardening

The Docker template no longer runs `docker compose up -d --build`, `docker build`, `docker pull`, or `docker run` against user-writable files. It only reads a localhost backend port from `.env` and writes nginx proxy configuration:

```
BACKEND_PORT=9100
```

Your container or compose stack must be started separately and listen on `127.0.0.1:BACKEND_PORT`.
